commit_reviews.summary: The commit discards a working modular Flask app (Blueprints, auth decorator, DB helpers) for a fresh "greenfield" rewrite, throwing away existing architecture instead of building on it.

problems: holds asyncio lock during broadcast sends
unsubscribe_all leaves empty-channel deletion inconsistent with subscribe
broadcast_channel snapshot may include duplicate client if subscribed to same channel twice
commit_reviews.summary: Adds channel pub/sub cleanly to the existing ClientRegistry pattern, with lock-protected state, matching method naming, consistent HTTP response style, and thorough async tests.
Reasonable transport abstraction over ClientRegistry that preserves async/type-hint conventions, but it leaks the private `_transport` attribute into the handler and ships no-op abstract hooks.
Adds rate limiting, /history endpoint, and TTL cleanup that follow the existing env-config and setter-injection patterns but leak some encapsulation.

problems: routing dispatch logic triplicated across RedisMessageBus and ClientRegistry
private attributes (_bus/_store) accessed across class boundaries in make_ws_handler/make_http_handler
missing type hints on some private methods (register/websocket
Redis channel-state consistency with in-process _channels not reconciled.
commit_reviews.summary: The commit cleanly layers SQLite persistence and optional Redis pub/sub on top of the existing ClientRegistry pattern, preserving the in-process fallback and message-envelope model.

compounding_issues: Monolith growth: app.py grew 170 → 729 lines over 5 sessions; the 'multi-file' seed structure was abandoned and no session ever split modules apart
Leaky coupling: ClientRegistry holds _bus/_store/_rate_limiter and handlers poke private attributes (reg._bus, reg._store) directly; S4 removed transport coupling but left this intact
Duplicated routing logic: broadcast/channel/direct dispatch is implemented in both ClientRegistry.persist_and_publish and RedisMessageBus.persist_and_publish, creating drift risk
Hand-rolled HTTP handler accumulates elif branches every session (/health, /messages, /history, /channels...) with repetitive f-string response blocks; extension debt grows monotonically
Incomplete abstraction: TRANSPORT env + _create_transport factory advertise multi-transport support but only WebSocketTransport exists
Minor: RateLimiter fails open (swallows exceptions → allows), and update_client_state uses stringly-typed if/elif action dispatch
key_decisions: Session 1 rewrote the Flask-auth seed entirely as a WebSocket notification server (greenfield) rather than layering onto the seed
Central ClientRegistry with in-memory client map guarded by asyncio.Lock became the core abstraction everything else builds on
Session 3's integration of Redis pub/sub (multi-instance scaling) + SQLite message persistence was the biggest architectural expansion
Session 3's handler-factory pattern (make_ws_handler(reg)/make_http_handler(reg)) enabled dependency injection and testability
Session 4's BaseTransport ABC + factory decoupled connection management from registry logic — the highest-quality structural decision
Session 5's operational layer (Redis rate limiter, TTL retention cleanup loop, filtered /history endpoint) reused the refactored store/bus interfaces cleanly
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality steadily improved with a clear sawtooth: Session 1 delivered a clean, focused single-file WS notification core; Session 2 extended it naturally with channels but began duplicating HTTP response code; Session 3 caused a complexity spike (app.py jumped to 543 lines) as persistence and a distributed bus were bolted on with growing coupling and dual code paths; Session 4 paid that debt down with the BaseTransport abstraction, restoring clarity through delegation; Session 5 layered rate limiting, retention, and history cleanly on top. The test suite grew in lockstep (61 passing, green at every commit), and each session preserved and extended the prior one's API surface rather than breaking it, so the arc reads as improving-with-a-midpoint-churn rather than flat or degrading.
story_review.summary: A coherent, well-paced 5-session build of a WebSocket notification service that progressed logically from core → channels → integration → transport refactor → operational concerns, marred only by a single-file monolith and lingering coupling between the registry, bus, store, and rate limiter.
